title: Information Correction, Memory Repair & Revision Atlas
purpose: Model how an information ecosystem discovers error, propagates correction, links revisions to old records and restores context without erasing history.

correction_types.meaning: A stated fact is changed because stronger evidence shows it was wrong.
Date, amount, identity, wording or scope becomes more exact without reversing the core claim.
The original fragment remains accurate but missing context materially changes interpretation.
An allegation, investigation, case, designation or scientific claim changes procedural/evidentiary status.
The facts remain but the archive's synthesis changes.
A source/owner withdraws a claim or analysis.
A newer record replaces an older operational version while preserving historical lineage.

repair_metrics.definition: Time from credible error detection to published correction.
Share of old public records that visibly link to the correction/revision.
Estimated overlap between people exposed to the original and correction.
Whether search/retrieval surfaces expose correction about as readily as the original.
Whether both original and corrected states remain reconstructable.
How many downstream copies/summaries are revised or annotated.
How often the obsolete claim continues appearing after correction.

memory_states.meaning: Accurate description of an earlier state that is no longer current.
Preserved earlier claim known to be wrong/incomplete, clearly annotated.
Operationally replaced by a newer representation.
Record persists without adequate provenance/context linkage.

repair_design_rules: Never delete history merely to make the current version look consistent.
Corrections should travel through the same discovery surfaces as adverse/original claims where feasible.
Search results and summaries should prefer current status while exposing historical state.
A corrected label should not persist indefinitely as unqualified identity.
Archive annotations should distinguish source correction from project reinterpretation.
Disputed claims should retain the dispute rather than be silently normalized into certainty.

concrete_cases.mechanism: Each edit creates a revision with identifiers, timestamps and metadata; users can inspect specific versions and compare revisions. Page moves preserve revision history.
repair_properties: current and prior versions can be compared
reverts create a new state rather than pretending the prior state never existed
visibility controls can restrict some deleted revision content
concrete_cases.lesson: A correction-friendly archive separates current truth/status from recoverable historical state.

concrete_cases.mechanism: Publishers can register editorially significant corrections, retractions and other updates as linked records; Crossmark exposes current status and update metadata to readers, including from PDFs when implemented.
repair_properties: update/retraction receives its own persistent record
metadata links the updating record to the affected record
current status can be exposed at retrieval time
concrete_cases.lesson: Memory repair can preserve the original while making changed status machine-readable and discoverable.

concrete_cases.mechanism: Creators are notified of many Community Guidelines removals/restrictions and can appeal; YouTube states an appeal triggers re-review and can result in an upheld or reversed decision, with appeals and reinstatements represented in its enforcement reporting.
repair_properties: adverse platform status can be challenged
concrete_cases.lesson: A platform correction system needs both reversal mechanics and visibility of the corrected status; an appeal channel alone does not guarantee retrieval parity for everyone who saw the original action.

design_patterns.rule: For materially significant changes, preserve the prior state and add a linked new state rather than silently overwriting history.
A correction/retraction should be discoverable from the original record and the update should identify exactly what it changes.
Default retrieval should expose current status while keeping historical state reconstructable.
Where feasible, corrections should propagate through the same discovery surfaces that carried the original claim or sanction.
